newsitem.title: NORWAY: A lackluster Norwegian share market holds flat.
newsitem.headline: A lackluster Norwegian share market holds flat.

text.p: Norwegian shares on Tuesday ignored a shaky start in the rest of Europe following Wall Street's overnight plunge, but a lack of fresh impulses and investor interest left the market flat.
Dealers said the market was expected to remain relatively calm for the next few weeks, baring any major news.

"We didn't pay any attention to Wall Street or the Japanese prime minister's comments because it was just phrases without any intent," said one broker. "But the volume is very low, the market has no momentum. Investors are waiting for the autumn."
Oslo's Total share index gained a slim 0.25 percent to end the session at 1,180.99 points. Turnover was a moderate 760 million crowns.
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro, the most traded share in turnover terms at 109 million crowns, advanced 3.50 crowns to 398 crowns. One dealer attributed the gain to a large buyer in the market.

Telecommunications company Nera closed almost four percent higher at 43 crowns in business worth 28 million crowns. Brokers said Nera was given upward momentum after breaking through a technical level to the upside at 42.20 crowns.
